impact: Impaired DNA double-strand break repair (BRCA1)
interpretation: Consumer-array detection of this selected BRCA1 variant is insufficient for clinical interpretation unless current ClinVar/ClinGen classification confirms pathogenicity. Treat as research-only / confirmation-required.

impact: Defective DNA homologous recombination repair
interpretation: Consumer-array detection of this selected BRCA1 variant is insufficient for clinical interpretation unless current ClinVar/ClinGen classification confirms pathogenicity. Treat as research-only / confirmation-required.

impact: BRCA2 truncation / double-strand DNA repair compromise
interpretation: ClinVar currently classifies this variant as benign for classic BRCA2-related hereditary breast/ovarian cancer predisposition. It may appear in literature as a low-penetrance modifier, but it must not be reported as a pathogenic BRCA2 mutation.

impact: APOE e4 isoform structural driver / LDL cholesterol elevations
interpretation: APOE rs429358 C-allele determines the e4 isoform. Combined with rs7412, it defines the APOE haplotype. One or two copies of e4 drive higher LDL cholesterol, elevated cardiovascular risk, and late-onset Alzheimer's susceptibility.

impact: APOE isoform determination (e2, e3, e4 haplotype)
interpretation: Determines the APOE e2 vs e3/e4 isoform. T/T at rs7412 combined with T/T at rs429358 defines e2/e2 (associated with lower LDL but risk of Type III hyperlipoproteinemia). G/G at rs7412 combined with C/C at rs429358 defines e4/e4.

impact: Altered cell cycle regulation in vascular walls
interpretation: The 9p21 non-coding region regulates vascular smooth muscle. The rs10757278 G allele is one of the most replicated risk markers for early-onset coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction, independent of lipid levels.

impact: Altered nitric oxide synthesis / vascular recovery
interpretation: NOS3 synthesizes nitric oxide, which regulates vasodilation and blood flow. The T (Asp) allele reduces enzyme function, potentially impairing endothelial nitric oxide production, athletic recovery, and arterial dilation under stress.

impact: Reduced nitric oxide synthase promoter transcription
interpretation: The C allele of rs2070744 is located in the NOS3 promoter, decreasing transcription rate. Associated with reduced basal nitric oxide production. Works synergistically with rs1799983 to affect vascular tone.

impact: Altered Type I collagen transcription / bone density reduction
interpretation: The COL1A1 Sp1 T-allele alters transcription factors, leading to a minor reduction in collagen Type I strength. It is replicated in studies showing reduced bone mineral density, osteopenic fracture risk, and soft-tissue injury susceptibility.

impact: Altered Type V collagen mRNA stability / tendon-ligament laxity
interpretation: COL5A1 rs12722 regulates Type V collagen, which controls fibril diameter in tendons and ligaments. The T allele is linked to mechanical property variations; C/C genotypes often display higher range of motion, while T/T has been associated with tendon injury susceptibility.

impact: Type III collagen protein structure variation
interpretation: COL3A1 Ala531Thr has been investigated in relation to tissue elasticity and pelvic/mitral valve laxity. It represents a common research variant, not a pathogenic mutation, and does not indicate vascular pathology.

impact: Reduced growth differentiation factor 5 expression / joint cartilage remodeling
interpretation: GDF5 is involved in joint development and cartilage repair. The T allele is associated with lower GDF5 promoter activity, showing a robust association with minor increases in osteoarthritis susceptibility (particularly knee and hip).

impact: Altered matrix metalloproteinase 3 expression / tissue remodeling
interpretation: MMP3 breaks down extracellular matrix. The 5A allele (represented by A) has higher transcription activity than 6A, altering matrix remodeling rates in tendons and ligaments. Replicated in studies of Achilles tendon injury risk.

impact: Fibrillin-1 structural integrity / aortic wall tension variation
interpretation: The FBN1 rs2118181 T allele is associated with increased susceptibility to sporadic thoracic aortic dissection and aneurysm in the general population, affecting baseline tissue elasticity. It is NOT diagnostic of syndromic Marfan syndrome.

impact: Fibrillin-1 microfibril structure / height variation
interpretation: FBN1 rs8033037 is a common variant investigated in genome-wide association studies for tall stature and bone elongation in the general population. It reflects minor, non-pathogenic variation in microfibril assembly.

impact: Alpha-actinin-3 deficiency / fast-twitch power reduction
interpretation: ACTN3 R577X. Homozygous T/T (X/X) results in complete deficiency of alpha-actinin-3 in fast muscle fibers. This shifts profile performance toward slow-twitch endurance, decreasing high-velocity sprint performance.

impact: Altered collagen XII expression / ACL injury risk
interpretation: COL12A1 rs970547 regulates Type XII collagen. The T allele is linked in association studies to altered baseline ligament properties, showing elevated susceptibility to ACL tears.

impact: Altered gelatinase B expression / matrix remodeling
interpretation: MMP9 regulates gelatinase B, which cleaves collagen Type IV. The T allele increases promoter activity, modifying extracellular matrix remodeling in cardiovascular tissues and joint cartilage.

impact: Reduced Diamine Oxidase (DAO) activity
interpretation: The AOC1 rs10156191 T allele is associated with lower DAO enzyme production. DAO is the primary enzyme responsible for breaking down ingested histamine in the gut. T-carriers may experience elevated sensitivity to high-histamine foods.

impact: Reduced Histamine N-Methyltransferase activity
interpretation: HNMT is responsible for intracellular histamine breakdown, particularly in the brain. The Thr105Ile T allele reduces enzyme activity, potentially prolonging intracellular histamine signals in the central nervous system.

impact: Lactase gene promoter downregulation (Lactose Intolerance)
interpretation: MCM6 regulates the LCT (lactase) gene. Homozygous C/C results in adult lactase non-persistence (lactose intolerance) in European populations. T-carriers (C/T or T/T) maintain lactase expression throughout adulthood.

impact: Altered satiety signaling / increased appetite susceptibility
interpretation: FTO rs9939609 is the most robust common obesity-risk locus. The A allele affects FTO expression, altering hypothalamus satiety signaling and increasing baseline appetite and food intake. Strongly modifiable by exercise and protein intake.

impact: Altered peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-gamma activity
interpretation: PPARG is a master regulator of fat cell development and insulin sensitivity. The G allele (Ala) is associated with improved insulin sensitivity and lower type 2 diabetes risk compared to the Pro/Pro genotype. A robust metabolic marker.

impact: Reduced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion
interpretation: KCNQ1 regulates potassium channels in pancreatic beta cells. The rs2237897 A allele is a robust marker associated with impaired insulin secretion following glucose loads, carrying a modest risk signal for type 2 diabetes.

impact: Impaired GLP-1 secretion / elevated type 2 diabetes risk
interpretation: TCF7L2 rs7903146 is the most significant common genetic risk locus for Type 2 Diabetes. The T allele is linked to reduced insulin secretion and impaired beta-cell response to GLP-1. Modifiable via low-glycemic index diets and exercise.

impact: Impaired zinc transport / reduced beta-cell insulin crystallization
interpretation: SLC30A8 is a zinc transporter in pancreatic beta cells. The C allele (Arg325) affects insulin storage and secretion kinetics, slightly increasing diabetes risk.

impact: Altered ATP-sensitive potassium channel activation
interpretation: KCNJ11 rs5219 (E23K variant, T allele) keeps the pancreatic beta-cell potassium channel open longer, decreasing insulin secretion in response to glucose.

impact: Altered glucokinase activity / triglyceride-glucose balance shift
interpretation: GCKR regulates glucokinase in the liver. The T allele is associated with lower fasting glucose but higher fasting triglycerides, illustrating a metabolic lipid-glucose partition tradeoff.

impact: Reduced APOA5 expression / elevated fasting triglycerides
interpretation: APOA5 rs662799 C allele is strongly associated with elevated serum triglycerides due to reduced clearing of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins.

impact: Altered Lipoprotein Lipase activity / triglyceride clearance
interpretation: LPL rs328 G-allele (Ser44Ter) causes premature truncation, resulting in increased LPL activity, leading to lower triglycerides and higher HDL.

impact: Altered cholesteryl ester transfer protein activity
interpretation: The A (TaqIB B2) allele of rs708272 is linked to decreased CETP expression, which increases protective HDL cholesterol levels.

impact: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) expression / atherosclerosis risk
interpretation: LPA rs10455872 is a robust promoter-associated SNP driving elevated levels of Lipoprotein(a). High Lp(a) levels are an independent, highly genetically determined risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

impact: APO(a) isoform reduction / elevated Lipoprotein(a)
interpretation: The rs3798220 C-allele is associated with smaller apolipoprotein(a) size isoforms, which are cleared slower, leading to elevated Lp(a) levels.

impact: Altered melanocortin-4 receptor expression / satiety regulation
interpretation: MC4R is a master hypothalamic regulator of energy homeostasis. The C allele is associated with minor satiety signaling impairments and higher baseline caloric intake.

impact: Altered glucocorticoid receptor sensitivity / HPA-axis stress response
interpretation: The FKBP5 rs1360780 T allele leads to higher induction of FKBP5, which reduces glucocorticoid receptor sensitivity, delaying negative feedback of cortisol during stress. Associated with stress sensitivity, PTSD, and major depression, particularly following early-life trauma.

impact: Altered serotonin 2A receptor expression
interpretation: The HTR2A A-1438G A allele has been studied for its potential to increase serotonin 2A receptor density. It is evaluated as a research-grade marker for emotional reactivity and atypical responses to serotonergic drugs.

impact: Altered oxytocin receptor sensitivity / social stress buffering
interpretation: The OXTR rs53576 A allele is studied in relation to social-emotional traits. A-carriers (AA/AG) may experience reduced oxytocin receptor sensitivity, affecting social support seeking and stress buffering under pressure.

impact: Lower monoamine oxidase A enzyme activity
interpretation: MAOA is responsible for clearing dopamine, serotonin, and norepinephrine. The rs6323 T allele represents a lower-activity enzyme, resulting in slower neurotransmitter clearance, which can lead to higher emotional reactivity under acute stress.

impact: Slower prefrontal dopamine & norepinephrine clearance
interpretation: COMT Val158Met. Homozygous A/A (Met/Met) decreases COMT enzyme activity up to 4-fold, leading to higher prefrontal dopamine levels. Associated with high cognitive focus and executive capacity, but increases stress and anxiety vulnerability ('Worrier' type).

impact: Reduced dopamine D2 receptor density
interpretation: DRD2 TaqIA (A1 allele, represented by T) is located in the adjacent ANKK1 gene and is associated with a 30-40% reduction in dopamine D2 receptor density in the striatum, potentially predisposing to reward-seeking behaviors and ADHD-like traits.

impact: Altered DRD2 mRNA stability & translation efficiency
interpretation: DRD2 C957T regulates translation efficiency and binding affinity of dopamine D2 receptors. The T allele is linked to differences in D2 receptor availability, which has been replicated in working memory and cognitive flexibility tasks.

impact: Neurodevelopmental cell adhesion / sensory processing traits
interpretation: CNTNAP2 is involved in neural migration and synaptic development. The T allele is evaluated as a research-grade marker linked to language development variation, sensory processing, and autism spectrum traits.

impact: Altered neuronal adhesion susceptibility
interpretation: MSNP1AS regulates neuronal structure. The T allele represents a minor research-level susceptibility variant replicated in broad neurodevelopmental studies, showing weak statistical correlation with autism spectrum traits.

impact: Altered prefrontal alpha-2A adrenergic receptor tone
interpretation: ADRA2A encodes the alpha-2A adrenergic receptor, which regulates norepinephrine in the prefrontal cortex. The G allele is linked to differences in receptor density and has been replicated in studies of methylphenidate response in ADHD.

impact: Estrogen receptor alpha transcriptional sensitivity
interpretation: The ESR1 Pvull G allele is a research-grade marker associated with altered transcriptional activity of estrogen receptor alpha, investigated in studies of mood fluctuations during rapid hormone drops.

impact: Estrogen receptor splicing / binding affinity variation
interpretation: ESR1 rs2234693 regulates receptor splicing. The T allele is evaluated as a research-grade marker linked to estrogen signaling sensitivity and emotional/physical symptoms during estrogen withdrawal.

impact: Progesterone receptor expression & sensitivity
interpretation: PGR rs8079626 A-carriers are evaluated in research regarding progesterone receptor sensitivity. Linked to mood fluctuations during the luteal progesterone spike.

impact: Reduced activity-dependent BDNF secretion
interpretation: The Met66 (A) allele reduces the activity-dependent release of Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor, which regulates synaptic plasticity and neurogenesis. Associated with alterations in episodic memory, working memory, and plasticity response to aerobic exercise.

impact: Increased anandamide levels / reduced FAAH expression
interpretation: FAAH degrades anandamide (the bliss molecule). The Thr129 (A) allele reduces enzyme activity, leading to elevated baseline anandamide. Associated with lower baseline anxiety, faster fear extinction, and decreased stress sensitivity.

impact: Altered adenosine receptor sensitivity / caffeine anxiety risk
interpretation: The T allele of rs5751876 is associated with increased susceptibility to caffeine-induced anxiety. Caffeine blocks ADORA2A receptors; carriers of the risk allele experience heightened sympathetic stimulation and panic responses.

impact: Altered mu-opioid receptor binding affinity / reward sensitivity
interpretation: The G (Asp) allele alters the mu-opioid receptor, reducing beta-endorphin binding affinity. Leads to minor reductions in pain sensitivity threshold but is associated in literature with altered reward seeking and higher social attachment demands.

impact: Reduced dopamine beta-hydroxylase expression / lower norepinephrine
interpretation: The DBH -1021C>T promoter T allele reduces the conversion of dopamine to norepinephrine. Homozygous T/T carriers have significantly lower plasma DBH activity, shifting dopamine-norepinephrine ratios in stress circuits.

impact: Reduced folate conversion efficiency (MTHFR)
interpretation: MTHFR C677T converts 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (active folate). Homozygous T/T reduces pathway efficiency by up to 70%, which can lead to elevated homocysteine if folate intake is inadequate.

impact: Secondary folate conversion pathway reduction
interpretation: MTHFR A1298C (G allele) causes a minor decrease in enzyme activity. Heterozygous C677T combined with A1298C (compound heterozygosity) decreases folate conversion by 40-50%, affecting one-carbon metabolism.

impact: Elevated baseline Interleukin-6 expression
interpretation: IL-6 is a key inflammatory cytokine. The G allele is linked to elevated baseline IL-6 secretion, which can influence systemic inflammatory tone and transient mood/cognitive sensitivity during immune activation.

impact: Increased Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha expression
interpretation: TNF-alpha is a master inflammatory cytokine. The rs1800629 A allele increases promoter transcription activity, linked to elevated TNF-alpha production and systemic baseline inflammatory susceptibility.

impact: Impaired iron clearance / elevated ferritin (Hemochromatosis risk)
interpretation: The HFE C282Y A allele prevents proper cell-surface expression of HFE, leading to unrestrained iron absorption. Homozygotes are at high risk of hereditary hemochromatosis, characterized by iron overload in organs.

impact: Impaired iron clearance / elevated ferritin (Hemochromatosis risk)
interpretation: H63D (G allele) is a milder modifier than C282Y. Compound heterozygosity (C282Y/H63D) can cause minor to moderate iron overload, while homozygous H63D/H63D rarely leads to severe clinical symptoms on its own.

impact: Altered methionine synthase activity / one-carbon methylation
interpretation: MTR encodes methionine synthase, which transfers a methyl group from folate to B12, then to homocysteine. The G allele is linked to minor enzyme velocity changes; verify B12/homocysteine status before supplementing.

impact: Altered methionine synthase reductase activity / B12 recycling
interpretation: MTRR is responsible for maintaining MTR in its active cob(I)alamin state. The G allele reduces recycling efficiency, slightly raising cobalamin demands.

impact: Altered transcobalamin-2 transport / B12 cellular uptake
interpretation: TCN2 is the primary transport protein for B12 from blood into tissues. The G (Arg) allele reduces binding affinity, which can lead to lower cellular delivery of B12 despite normal serum B12 levels.

impact: Non-secretor status / lower serum vitamin B12 levels
interpretation: FUT2 controls the secretion of ABH blood group antigens into body fluids. Homozygous A/A results in 'non-secretor' status, which alters gut microbiome composition and is strongly linked to lower circulating serum B12 levels.

impact: Reduced phosphatidylcholine synthesis / elevated choline demand
interpretation: PEMT synthesizes phosphatidylcholine in the liver. The T (Met) allele reduces enzyme activity, making carriers highly susceptible to choline deficiency, fatty liver (NAFLD), and muscle damage on low-choline diets.

impact: Altered folate pathway enzymes / elevated choline requirement
interpretation: MTHFD1 rs2236225 regulates a trifunctional folate enzyme. The A (His) allele impairs folate-mediated one-carbon flow, increasing dependence on the alternative choline-dependent (BHMT) pathway in the liver.

impact: Altered Vitamin D receptor structural transcription
interpretation: The FokI T (f) allele creates a longer, slightly less active VDR protein isoform. T-carriers may require slightly higher vitamin D3 levels to achieve comparable transcription of downstream target genes.

impact: Altered Vitamin D receptor levels
interpretation: BsmI is an intronic polymorphism that acts as a proxy for VDR expression level variations. The A (b) allele is frequently linked in association studies to lower VDR density.

impact: Reduced Vitamin D-binding protein / lower circulating D3
interpretation: GC encodes Vitamin D-binding protein (DBP). The C allele is associated with lower DBP levels and is the most robust GWAS locus driving reduced circulating serum 25(OH)D levels in the population.

impact: Impaired Vitamin D 25-hydroxylation efficiency
interpretation: CYP2R1 is the primary liver enzyme that converts Vitamin D3 into circulating 25(OH)D. The A allele reduces enzyme activity, leading to less efficient conversion of dietary or sun-derived D3.

impact: Impaired skin synthesis of pre-vitamin D3
interpretation: DHCR7 converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol, regulating the precursor pool for Vitamin D3 synthesis in the skin. The T allele is linked to reduced efficiency in synthesizing vitamin D3 from UVB light.

impact: Reduced/Inactive CYP2D6 enzyme activity
interpretation: CYP2D6*4 is a well-established loss-of-function allele. Homozygous A/A results in a poor metabolizer phenotype, leading to impaired clearance and elevated levels of dextromethorphan (DXM), atomoxetine, and many antidepressants, while reducing the activation of codeine/tramadol.

impact: Reduced CYP2C9 enzyme clearance
interpretation: The CYP2C9*3 variant significantly reduces enzymatic clearance. C-carriers may experience slower clearance and higher systemic levels of warfarin, statins, and common NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or celecoxib).

impact: Reduced CYP2C9 enzyme clearance
interpretation: CYP2C9*2 (rs1799853) is a common coding variant that reduces enzyme activity. Individuals carrying T-alleles metabolize warfarin, phenytoin, and NSAIDs slower than typical *1/*1 individuals.

impact: Ultra-rapid CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism
interpretation: The CYP2C19*17 variant is associated with increased transcription. T-carriers are ultra-rapid metabolizers of SSRI antidepressants (like escitalopram and sertraline) and proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), potentially leading to lower drug efficacy at standard doses.

impact: Reduced CYP2C19 enzyme activity (loss of function)
interpretation: CYP2C19*2 is a common loss-of-function allele. Homozygous carriers have poor metabolizer status, leading to reduced activation of clopidogrel and slow clearance of certain SSRIs and PPIs.

impact: Reduced CYP2C19 enzyme activity (loss of function)
interpretation: CYP2C19*3 is a loss-of-function allele that introduces a premature stop codon. Primarily observed in East Asian populations, homozygosity or compound heterozygosity results in a poor metabolizer phenotype.

impact: Impaired statin transport / elevated systemic statin levels
interpretation: The SLCO1B1 Val174Ala C allele decreases the transport of statins (especially simvastatin) into the liver, resulting in higher blood concentrations and a significantly higher risk of statin-induced myopathy (muscle pain).

impact: Slower caffeine clearance rate
interpretation: CYP1A2*1F C-carriers (A/C or C/C) are slow caffeine metabolizers. Slower clearance prolongs caffeine's systemic effects, increasing the risk of sleep disruption, anxiety, and cardiovascular stress under heavy caffeine intake.

impact: Increased sensitivity to warfarin
interpretation: The VKORC1 -1639G>A promoter variant decreases VKORC1 expression. Individuals with the A allele require significantly lower therapeutic warfarin doses to avoid bleeding risks.

impact: Altered Vitamin K metabolism / higher warfarin dose requirements
interpretation: The Met433 variant reduces CYP4F2 activity, causing lower breakdown of Vitamin K. Consequently, T-carriers require slightly higher doses of warfarin to achieve anticoagulation.

impact: Impaired CYP3A5 enzyme activity (non-expressor)
interpretation: Homozygosity for the CYP3A5*3 C-allele causes a splicing defect and lack of active enzyme. Carriers of *3/*3 are CYP3A5 'non-expressors', leading to slower clearance of drugs like tacrolimus, midazolam, and certain statins.

impact: Reduced CYP2B6 metabolism
interpretation: The CYP2B6*6 variant is associated with reduced enzyme activity and expression. Carriers of the T allele may experience slow clearance of bupropion (Wellbutrin), methadone, and efavirenz, leading to elevated drug exposure.

impact: Impaired drug transport / statin toxicity risk / gout susceptibility
interpretation: The ABCG2 Gln141Lys T allele impairs active transport of substrates, resulting in elevated systemic levels of statins (specifically rosuvastatin) and reduced renal uric acid export, increasing gout risk.

impact: Severe fluorouracil / capecitabine toxicity risk (loss of function)
interpretation: DPYD*2A is a critical splice-site variant leading to complete lack of DPD enzyme activity. Carriers of the A allele are at extreme risk of life-threatening toxicity (neutropenia, severe mucosal inflammation) if treated with standard doses of fluorouracil or capecitabine.

impact: Severe fluorouracil / capecitabine toxicity risk (loss of function)
interpretation: The I560S variant is a rare DPYD allele that causes a severe reduction in DPD enzyme clearance. Carriers of the A allele require alternative cancer therapies or drastic dose reductions to prevent severe systemic toxicity.

impact: Severe fluorouracil / capecitabine toxicity risk (loss of function)
interpretation: The Y186C variant causes intermediate to poor DPD clearance. A-carriers have a high susceptibility to severe adverse events from 5-FU based chemotherapy regimens.

impact: Impaired TPMT enzyme activity (thiopurine toxicity)
interpretation: TPMT*3C is a primary coding variant that reduces activity of the thiopurine S-methyltransferase enzyme. Carriers of the C allele are susceptible to severe, potentially fatal bone marrow toxicity (myelosuppression) under standard doses of azathioprine or mercaptopurine.

impact: Impaired TPMT enzyme activity (thiopurine toxicity)
interpretation: The TPMT*3A allele contains two mutations (rs1142345 and rs1800460). Homozygous carriers have nearly zero TPMT activity and require extremely reduced dosing (e.g. 10% of typical dose) of thiopurines.

impact: Severe thiopurine-induced myelosuppression (loss of function)
interpretation: NUDT15 rs116855232 is a major loss-of-function allele, highly prevalent in East Asian populations. Homozygotes or compound heterozygotes develop severe leucopenia and alopecia under thiopurines, independent of TPMT status.

impact: Reduced Adenosine Deaminase activity / elevated sleep pressure
interpretation: ADA breaks down adenosine (the sleep-pressure molecule). The rs73598374 A allele reduces ADA activity. A-carriers accumulate adenosine slower but have higher baseline levels, leading to deeper sleep and more slow-wave activity, but potentially higher morning sleep inertia.

impact: Circadian rhythm phase shifting / sleep fragmentation
interpretation: PER2 is a core clock gene. The rs934945 A allele has been associated with sleep schedule disruptions, night awakenings, and anxious dreams in small clinical cohorts. A research-grade chronotype marker.

impact: Altered circadian clock speed / eveningness preference
interpretation: The CLOCK 3111C allele is robustly associated with eveningness chronotype ('night owl') and elevated sleep latency. Individuals carrying the C allele may experience delayed melatonin secretion onset.

impact: Reduced melatonin receptor density / impaired morning insulin release
interpretation: MTNR1B rs10830963 G allele drives increased expression of melatonin receptors on pancreatic islet cells, causing prolonged inhibition of insulin secretion during the morning when melatonin is high. Explains circadian-metabolic glucose mismatch.

impact: Reduced intracellular T4-to-T3 thyroid hormone conversion
interpretation: DIO2 converts inactive T4 into active T3 inside cells. The G (Ala) allele is linked to reduced conversion efficiency, which may contribute to localized tissue hypothyroid symptoms (fatigue, brain fog) despite normal serum TSH levels.

impact: Reduced selenium-dependent glutathione peroxidase activity
interpretation: GPX1 is a key antioxidant enzyme that protects the thyroid gland from hydrogen peroxide during hormone synthesis. The T (Leu) allele reduces enzyme activity, increasing thyroid oxidative stress vulnerability, particularly if selenium status is low.

impact: Altered T-cell activation regulation / autoimmune susceptibility
interpretation: CTLA-4 is an immune checkpoint receptor. The G (Ala) allele reduces CTLA-4 cell surface expression, leading to elevated T-cell activation and increased baseline predisposition to autoimmune conditions including thyroiditis.

impact: Impaired lymphoid phosphatase regulation / autoimmune risk modifier
interpretation: PTPN22 Arg620Trp (T allele) alters a tyrosine phosphatase, which compromises T-cell receptor signaling inhibition. Associated with elevated risks of systemic lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes, and autoimmune thyroiditis.

impact: Altered CD40 translation / thyroid antibody production
interpretation: The C allele of the CD40 -1C>T translation start site variant increases translation efficiency, promoting B-cell activation and elevating baseline levels of thyroid antibodies in susceptible individuals.

impact: Altered thyroid stimulating hormone receptor expression
interpretation: The TSHR rs179247 A allele is a replicated risk modifier associated with autoimmune thyroid diseases (such as Graves' disease and Hashimoto's), affecting receptor signaling sensitivity.

impact: Altered T4-to-T3 deiodination in liver/kidneys
interpretation: DIO1 is responsible for baseline peripheral deiodination. The C allele is linked to shifts in Free T4/Free T3 ratios in serum, reflecting minor variations in systemic conversion velocity.
